scandals.title: Fake bank accounts / money-laundering case — Zardari Group, Omni Group, and Bahria Town
scandals.summary: Following a 2015 FIA tip-off about suspicious transactions at Summit Bank, Sindh Bank and United Bank Limited, the Supreme Court took suo motu notice in 2018 and ordered a Joint Investigation Team (JIT) to probe an alleged network of fake bank accounts used to launder money. The JIT found that dozens of fictitious accounts (initially 29, later expanding to dozens more) held by fake entities had moved at least Rs42 billion, later cited as approximately Rs220 billion across a wider set of accounts and individuals, alleging a close nexus between the Zardari Group, Omni Group (owned by Zardari associate Anwar Majeed) and Bahria Town, funneling kickbacks and commissions from contractors. Former president Asif Ali Zardari, his sister Faryal Talpur, Omni Group's Anwar Majeed and Abdul Ghani Majeed, and banker Hussain Lawai were among those named; several were arrested and the Supreme Court froze Omni Group's assets. Zardari was arrested by NAB in June 2019 and later released on bail. The case was eventually transferred to a special banking court in Karachi; in a final charge-sheet, 14 individuals including Faryal Talpur were placed in Column Two (indicating insufficient evidence) and released, with the court accepting her explanation that funds attributed to her were legitimate sugarcane-sale proceeds from family farms.
scandals.institution: Federal Investigation Agency / National Accountability Bureau / Special Court (Offences in Banks)
scandals.amount_notes: The JIT's initial finding (December 2018) was that 29 fake accounts laundered approximately Rs42 billion; the investigation subsequently expanded to cover roughly Rs220 billion in transactions across a much larger set of accounts, individuals and entities as more accounts and companies were identified. No single court-adjudicated final loss figure was located.

scandals.title: Bahria Town Karachi land case — Rs460 billion Supreme Court settlement and UK NCA £190m recovery
scandals.summary: The Supreme Court held in 2018 that land granted by the Sindh government to the Malir Development Authority, and its subsequent exchange with private developer Bahria Town for its Bahria Town Karachi housing project, was illegal. In March 2019 the Court accepted a Rs460 billion settlement offer from Bahria Town in lieu of prosecution, staying a threatened NAB reference. Separately, the UK's National Crime Agency reached a civil £190 million settlement in December 2019 with the family of Bahria Town owner Malik Riaz over suspected proceeds of crime, without a criminal conviction. Part of the NCA-recovered funds (~£140m) was routed to a Supreme Court account rather than directly to the federal government, prompting further Supreme Court scrutiny in 2023 over incomplete settlement payments (only ~Rs60.72bn of Rs460bn had been paid by October 2023) and irregular remittance channels. As of 2025, NAB had frozen Bahria Town-linked properties and pursued asset auctions amid non-payment, contested in the Islamabad High Court.

scandals.title: LNG Terminal-1 (Engro/EETL) contract reference — Shahid Khaqan Abbasi and others

scandals.title: Toshakhana reference — Imran Khan state-gifts case
scandals.summary: The Election Commission of Pakistan (ECP) and later a NAB/FIA-linked criminal reference alleged that then-prime minister Imran Khan retained and sold, at officially discounted prices, state gifts (including watches, a ring, a pen and cufflinks) received from foreign dignitaries and stored in the Toshakhana, without properly declaring the proceeds — allegedly profiting him over Rs36 million. The ECP disqualified Khan under Article 63(1)(p) in October 2022 for making false statements in his asset declarations. A second, related NAB/FIA reference ('Toshakhana-II'), covering additional gifts and alleging his wife Bushra Bibi's involvement, followed Khan's arrest in July 2024; that case was transferred from NAB to an FIA special court after 2024 accountability-law amendments. As of the most recent located reporting, Supreme Court appeals concerning the original Toshakhana conviction remained pending.

scandals.title: Bus Rapid Transit (BRT) Peshawar project — contract irregularities inquiry
scandals.summary: Following years of delays and cost escalation on the Asian Development Bank-funded Peshawar BRT mass-transit project, the Peshawar High Court ordered NAB in July 2018 to investigate alleged illegal contract awards and cost overruns; a parallel FIA probe was later also ordered but both were repeatedly stayed by the Supreme Court after the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa government's appeals. NAB's investigation, which gained pace under new leadership after 2022, found that six major civil-works contracts had been awarded to joint ventures whose named international partners did not actually perform the work, that contractors had submitted bogus bank guarantees and fraudulent audit reports, and that a 20% rate premium was paid for international involvement that never materialised. Rather than pursuing a criminal reference, NAB negotiated an indirect settlement: contractors withdrew a Rs31.5 billion claim pending at the International Court of Arbitration and the project was completed within its original cost framework, which NAB announced in September 2024 as an aggregate 'recovery/saving' of Rs168.5 billion — its largest such figure in 25 years.

scandals.title: Bank of Punjab (BoP) loan fraud case — Hamesh Khan and Haris Steel Mills
scandals.summary: NAB alleged that Bank of Punjab president Hamesh Khan, in connivance with Haris Steel Industries CEO Sheikh Muhammad Afzal and other bank officials, sanctioned billions of rupees in loans between 2005 and 2007 against inadequate or falsified collateral — most notably an approximately Rs8.4 billion facility to Haris Steel Mills — while the bank simultaneously submitted falsified performance reports to the State Bank of Pakistan, masking losses as profits through fake audits and window-dressing of accounts. NAB filed a reference on 27 September 2007 against 12 accused, alleging a core Rs9 billion fraud; a 2010 NAB estimate put total corruption in the bank at roughly Rs76 billion. Hamesh Khan fled to the United States in March 2008 while under investigation, was arrested there on an Interpol red notice, and was extradited to Pakistan. After a 17-year prosecution, NAB moved in November 2024 to withdraw the reference against Khan and Sheikh Afzal, citing insufficient evidence — a request the Bank of Punjab itself opposed in court.

scandals.title: Billion Tree Tsunami Project (KP) — audit and NAB irregularities inquiry
scandals.summary: The Khyber Pakhtunkhwa government's flagship Billion Tree Tsunami afforestation project, launched in November 2014, faced a series of official inquiries into procurement and plantation irregularities. A KP Assembly parliamentary committee investigating in 2019 backed opposition allegations of exaggerated plantation figures after visiting sites in Bannu. Separate Auditor General of Pakistan special audits found irregularities of Rs410 million (2020 report, citing an unmet 36% plantation target and Rs299.29 million in seedling overpayments) and later Rs3.49 billion (2022 report, including Rs195.7 million in unaccounted-for plants and Rs109.365 million in losses from uncertified seeds). NAB's initial complaint-verification inquiry, opened in 2018, found approximately Rs462 million in suspected embezzlement — including Rs359.01 million in farm-forestry plant embezzlement — and recommended it be converted into a full investigation with several sub-inquiries against KP Forest Department officials. Over 300 KP forest officials were reported suspended or dismissed over the project's irregularities.

scandals.title: ARY Gold reference — alleged kickbacks for exclusive gold and silver import rights
scandals.summary: NAB alleged that Dubai-based bullion trader Abdul Razzak Yaqoob, owner of ARY Gold, paid bribes to secure exclusive rights to import and trade gold and silver in Pakistan during the 1990s, with funds allegedly routed through Swiss lawyer Jens Schlegelmilch's Capricorn Trading entity, in which Asif Ali Zardari held a beneficial interest. NAB's reference named then-president Asif Ali Zardari, ARY Gold's owner Haji Abdul Razzaq, former commerce secretary Brig (retd) Aslam Hayat Qureshi, former finance secretary Javed Talaat, and others, alleging that the licences of two existing gold/silver import companies were illegally cancelled to clear the way for ARY Gold. In July 2011, an accountability court acquitted five of the accused — including Zardari's principal secretary Salman Farooqi, Qureshi, and ARY Gold's owners — for lack of proven evidence, while issuing permanent arrest warrants and proclaimed-offender status for Javed Talaat and Jens Schlegelmilch, who did not appear before the court. The case against Zardari himself did not proceed to trial due to presidential immunity during his tenure.

scandals.title: Pakistan Railways locomotive spare parts procurement scam
scandals.summary: NAB investigated the procurement of spare parts for 69 Chinese-made locomotives purchased by Pakistan Railways during 2001-02, alleging that a negotiation committee headed by General Manager (Maintenance & Services) Naeem Malik purchased spare parts worth $15.6 million at grossly inflated prices — with 356 items procured at roughly five times open-market price, 256 items at double price, and 776 items at other inflated rates — causing substantial loss to the exchequer. NAB separately filed a related Rs340 million case over repair of the same 69 locomotives against former general manager Saeed Akhtar, who was also implicated in a separate Pakistan Railways scrap-disposal scandal.

scandals.title: 2019-2020 wheat flour crisis — FIA inquiry into procurement failures and Sindh stock pilferage
scandals.summary: A nationwide wheat flour shortage that began in late 2019 and peaked in January 2020 prompted the federal government to task the FIA with an inquiry into its causes. The FIA report, submitted to Prime Minister Imran Khan in April 2020, found the crisis stemmed from poor planning and a 2.5-million-tonne (35%) shortfall against public procurement targets — Sindh procured zero tonnes against a one-million-tonne target and Punjab procured only 3.315 million tonnes against a four-million-tonne target — compounded by delayed wheat collection and flour-mill malpractices. The inquiry assigned responsibility to the then-federal food secretary and Punjab's ex-director food for missed procurement targets, and to provincial food ministers for inadequate policy response. Separately, the report noted that when Sindh claimed a carry-forward stock of 0.98 million tonnes, NAB found evidence of massive pilferage and theft from Sindh's wheat stocks, casting doubt on the province's reported reserves.

scandals.title: Nandipur Power Project — delay, cost-escalation and corruption reference
scandals.summary: The Nandipur combined-cycle power project, initiated in 2005 with an original budget of roughly Rs22-27 billion, was beset by years of delays — including a 2012 contract termination by Chinese contractor Dongfang Electric Corporation over machinery stuck at Karachi port — that pushed its final cost to approximately Rs58.42 billion. A Supreme Court-appointed one-man commission led by retired Justice Rehmat Hussain Jafri concluded in 2013 that the national exchequer suffered a colossal Rs113 billion loss due to delays attributable to the federal law ministry, while a later Auditor General of Pakistan audit found more than Rs80 billion in irregularities. The plant, when finally commissioned in 2015, broke down within days and was found to produce electricity at roughly Rs42 per unit — far above cheaper legacy plants — leading to its shutdown. The Supreme Court ordered NAB to investigate in 2018, and NAB filed a reference in March 2018 against seven individuals, including former law minister Babar Awan and former prime minister Raja Pervez Ashraf, alleging a Rs27 billion loss from delayed approvals. An accountability court acquitted Babar Awan and former law secretary Riaz Kiyani in June 2019, while rejecting Raja Pervez Ashraf's acquittal plea; the Islamabad High Court upheld Awan's acquittal in January 2021, ruling that the Supreme Court-ordered commission had found negligence, not corruption.
scandals.institution: Ministry of Water and Power / Ministry of Law and Justice
scandals.amount_notes: The Justice Jafri commission (2013) found a Rs113bn exchequer loss from delays; a later AGP audit separately found over Rs80bn in irregularities; NAB's 2018 criminal reference alleged a narrower Rs27bn loss specifically from delayed approvals.
